summary: Some Slack recipients missing from alert deliveries when org has both webhook and Slack app integrations
description: Issue summary: Customer reports missing Slack recipients for scheduled alerts. Impact: Some team members did not receive critical alert notifications for ~24 hours, leading to delayed incident response. Environment: prod/us-east (KestrelAI org), org has both an incoming-webhook configured and an OAuth Slack App integration for notifications. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create an alert on a dashboard that targets multiple Slack channels/users via both webhook URL and app-based channel ID. 2) Save schedule and wait for next evaluation. 3) Observe Delivery logs and Slack channel mention history. Observed: Alert delivery log shows a single aggregated recipient list after dedupe; actual delivered notifications only landed to the webhook channel, app-based targets were omitted. Expected: Both webhook-based and app-based targets should be notified independently. Logs/screenshots: Delivery log snippet and customer-provided Slack audit timestamps attached in comments.
steps_to_reproduce: Create alert with two Slack targets: a legacy incoming webhook URL and a Slack App channel target (app-scoped channel ID).
Trigger alert rule evaluation (use a short schedule) and check Notification Delivery logs in Console > Alerting > Recent Deliveries.
Compare 'recipients' field in delivery event vs actual messages in Slack workspace audit logs.
observed_behavior: Notification delivery events show a de-duplicated recipient array with normalized values.
Only webhook channel received a message; app-scoped channel entries were dropped by notification worker prior to sending.
expected_behavior: All configured Slack targets receive the alert independently.
Delivery event recipients should reflect exact configured targets (no unintended normalization).
investigation_notes: Initial triage (2026-03-09): Support confirmed customer has both integration types; reproduced in staging by creating same config.

Notification worker code normalizes Slack targets by stripping query params and lowercasing URL/identifiers to dedupe duplicates (introduced in PR 4321 to reduce duplicate messages when same endpoint added twice).

Normalization logic conflates webhook URLs and app channel identifiers when both include same trailing token pattern (example: webhook URL and app 'incoming' token share a substring), causing dedupe to drop app entries.
Delivery logs show recipient_hash collision for webhook and app target: both map to same normalized key 'slack:incoming:abc123'.
SRE ran a targeted test injecting both target types and confirmed worker resolves to single send job.
logs_and_artifacts: slack_audit: 2026-03-09T14:02:10Z - message_posted - channel: C04566WHQ (webhook), no message found for app-based channel C09X12ABC
workaround: Temporarily configure only one type of Slack target per alert (prefer app integration) to ensure alerts reach intended recipients.
As a stopgap, create duplicate alert rules each targeting a single integration type until fix is deployed.
resolution: Root cause: over-aggressive deduplication normalization in notification worker conflating webhook URLs and app-scoped channel identifiers.
Fix: adjust normalization algorithm to include integration-type prefix (webhook vs app) and preserve full token segments for app channel ids. Implemented in PR 4862.
Deployment: PR merged to main on 2026-03-11; rolling deploy to notification-worker fleet completed 2026-03-12 03:20 UTC with canary in us-east then global rollout.
Post-deploy validation: Re-ran staging and prod repros; delivery events now list distinct recipients and both webhook + app channels receive messages.
Customer confirmation: KestrelAI verified delivery for missed alerts and confirmed no further misses observed on 2026-03-12.
postmortem_followup: Add unit/integration tests covering combinations of webhook URLs and app channel IDs to prevent regression (owner: notifications eng).
Create dashboard alerted on recipient_hash_collision rate spike to catch normalization regressions early (owner: observability).
Run targeted backfill to re-send high-priority alerts that were omitted between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-09 (owner: support ops).
Customer-facing note: prepare short summary for KestrelAI and add to support ticket once backfill completes.
